title: Anything That Can Go Wrong, Will
coreMove: Stress-test a plan by asking what behavior its metric rewards, how the fix could backfire, and what future capability the plan may be borrowing from.
sourcePressure: The source uses Murphy’s Law, perverse incentives, cobra effect, short-termism, and market failure to show how systems can produce unintended outcomes even from plausible plans.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using Murphy’s Law as fatalism instead of as a disciplined search for incentives, loopholes, and delayed costs.

sourceAnchors.name: Atlanta high-stakes testing culture
sourceAnchors.detail: the source cites adults correcting student answers when standardized-score pressure became the rewarded target
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Atlanta matters because the score stopped being a signal and became the thing adults were paid, praised, or punished to move.

sourceAnchors.name: hospital and college rankings
sourceAnchors.detail: the source notes rankings pressure as another setting where measurement can redirect behavior
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A ranking can begin as a mirror and end as a steering wheel.

counterintuition: The fix can become the problem
tryThisNow: List three ways your plan could fail
examples: support team ticket quota with banned Priya
quarterly training cuts copied from old draft

exampleSpecs.domain: Hannah, a public-library director rewarding branches for raw checkout volume
exampleSpecs.audience: civic managers tempted by clean output metrics
exampleSpecs.stakes: staff may push popular repeats while neglecting literacy outreach
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hannah moves the proposed leaderboard beside the mission statement and adds outreach-quality checks before the metric goes live
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminate leaderboard propped against a cart of returned picture books

exampleSpecs.domain: Luca, a restaurant group owner offering bonuses for the lowest food waste
exampleSpecs.audience: operators who use incentives to fix cost leaks
exampleSpecs.stakes: chefs might under-prep and disappoint dinner guests to protect the bonus
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luca predicts the loophole, watches one kitchen run out of salmon before nine, and rewrites the bonus around waste plus sellout complaints
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the ice drawer smells clean because the salmon tray is already empty

exampleSpecs.domain: Ingrid, a university residence coordinator using stricter quiet-hour penalties after noise complaints spike
exampleSpecs.audience: student-life leaders balancing rules and adaptation
exampleSpecs.stakes: students may move parties off-site into riskier settings
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid asks resident assistants where noise will go after the fine doubles and changes the plan to include late common-room programming
exampleSpecs.firstImage: “Where do they go when this fine works?”

exampleSpecs.domain: Tomás, a factory maintenance lead told to postpone lubrication checks to hit the monthly output target
exampleSpecs.stakes: a prettier month could buy a line stoppage next quarter
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tomás places the output target next to the bearing-failure log and refuses the cut that would spend machine health for monthly volume
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 5:40 a.m., Tomás hears the press line change pitch

exampleSpecs.domain: Layla, a nonprofit grants manager designing a donor target for families housed within thirty days
exampleSpecs.audience: mission-driven readers wary of metric capture
exampleSpecs.stakes: caseworkers might favor easy placements and leave harder families waiting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Layla reviews the first month, separates fast placements from hard-case neglect, and adds a weighted metric before the distortion becomes culture
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Layla one month to see the missing families were not missing by accident
mustAvoid: school testing anchor as fictional example

exampleSpecs.domain: Pavel, a city bike-share planner considering a bounty for abandoned bikes returned to docks
exampleSpecs.audience: public-service readers designing interventions in open systems
exampleSpecs.stakes: the bounty could encourage people to move bikes out of docks just to collect returns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pavel sketches the bounty loop, spots the cobra-effect path, and changes the reward to verified staff-reported recoveries
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What happens if the reward creates the abandoned bike?

tryThisNowSpec: For one plan you are about to reward or measure, write the sentence “People will get more of this by…” and finish it with the worst plausible behavior the metric could invite.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

skillTargets: identify the chapter-specific model in a fresh scenario for Anything That Can Go Wrong, Will
choose the visible action that performs the core move rather than naming the concept
explain the failure mode that appears when the model is used generically
evaluate tradeoffs and limits without sliding into certainty, cynicism, or manipulation

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
